quizzes.title: Defence and Border Infrastructure: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Defence was a major area of focus in this month's current affairs. The Kalam & Kavach 3.0 Defence Conference was described as a high-level platform for deliberations on India's defence transformation, military modernisation and future preparedness. The conference brings defence themes into one forum, and the booklet treats it as a significant event for the sector. Another entry under the defence heading is the TARA weapon system. The booklet describes TARA as a glide weapon system developed in India, and it reports a recent trial of the system as a step in the country's defence progress. Each entry is written in short points, so readers can follow the key terms and the main features quickly. The booklet also covers border infrastructure under the same heading. The Border Roads Organisation is named as the body for this work, and it is discussed together with Project Deepak. The entries are kept brief, and the booklet gives the main terms and details for each item in a few lines. Together, these entries give a snapshot of defence news from the month. They describe a conference, a weapon system and a border agency, and each is presented as a separate point. Each point stands on its own, so the entries can be read in any order.

questions.q: What position does the booklet give TARA among India's indigenous glide weapon systems?
questions.explanation: The booklet calls TARA India's first indigenous glide weapon system.

questions.q: In which year was the Border Roads Organisation established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Border Roads Organisation was established in 1960.

questions.q: Which ministry organised the Kalam & Kavach 3.0 Defence Conference?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the conference was organised by the Ministry of Defence.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. TARA   ->   A. Western Himalayas
II. Project Deepak   ->   B. Jointness, Aatmanirbharta and Innovation
III. Border Roads Organisation   ->   C. Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation
IV. JAI   ->   D. Premier agency for border infrastructure
Which of the following is the correct matching?
questions.explanation: TARA stands for Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation, Project Deepak is in the Western Himalayas, the BRO is the premier agency for border infrastructure, and JAI stands for Jointness, Aatmanirbharta and Innovation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Border Roads Organisation works in high-altitude and strategically sensitive areas.
Reason (R): The Border Roads Organisation has its headquarters in New Delhi.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are supported by the booklet, but the headquarters location does not explain the kind of areas where the organisation works.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Kalam & Kavach 3.0 conference was the second edition of the event.
II. The conference was held in New Delhi.
III. TARA's modular range-extension kit can be attached to an existing unguided warhead.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the booklet calls it the 3rd edition, while statements II and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Kalam & Kavach 3.0 conference was held in Mumbai.
II. DRDO and the Indian Air Force conducted the maiden flight trial of TARA.
III. Project Deepak was launched in 1980.
questions.explanation: Only statement II matches the booklet, since the conference was held in New Delhi and Project Deepak is dated 1961.

quizzes.title: Defence and Border Infrastructure: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: The defence sector featured prominently in the May 2026 Ailet Corner section of the booklet. Its opening entry concerns the Kalam & Kavach 3.0 conference, which is described as a high-level platform for discussing India's defence transformation, military modernisation and future preparedness. The booklet gives the conference a short description and lists its main points briefly. Another entry covers the TARA weapon system. The booklet describes it as an indigenous glide weapon, meaning a system developed within India. Several points about the system are listed in short form, including its trial and the agencies that took part in it. Border infrastructure forms the third part of this defence coverage. The Border Roads Organisation is presented as India's premier agency for this work, and its activities are described as taking place in difficult terrain. Project Deepak is listed under the same heading, and the booklet mentions it alongside the organisation's wider work on the country's borders. Each entry is a self-contained point, so the section can be read in any order. The booklet presents the Kalam & Kavach entry first, followed by the weapon system and then the border infrastructure entries. Short descriptions and headings make each item easy to find on the page.

questions.q: In which year was the Border Roads Organisation established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Border Roads Organisation was established in 1960.

questions.q: Which ministry organised the Kalam & Kavach 3.0 Defence Conference? (ministry name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Ministry of Defence as the organiser of the conference.

questions.q: What does the acronym TARA stand for? (full phrase)
questions.explanation: The booklet expands TARA as Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation.

questions.q: Which region does Project Deepak operate in? (region name)
questions.explanation: The booklet places Project Deepak in the Western Himalayas.

questions.q: In which city is the headquarters of the Border Roads Organisation located? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the headquarters of the Border Roads Organisation as New Delhi.

questions.q: Which edition of the Kalam & Kavach Defence Conference is described in this booklet? (ordinal)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the event as the 3rd edition of the conference.

questions.q: What is the name of the kit that attaches to an existing unguided warhead to convert it into a precision-guided weapon? (name of kit)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes TARA's modular range-extension kit as the attachment that converts an unguided warhead into a precision-guided weapon.

quizzes.title: Governance, Crime Data and Remembrance: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: The May 2026 Ailet Corner section of the booklet covers governance, crime data and remembrance. Its governance item is a skilling programme for the creative sector, which aims to build AI capabilities that are ready for industry. The programme aims to strengthen India's creative economy and digital content ecosystem, and its target areas include media and animation. The programme is described as a way to build digital skills for people working in creative industries. Crime data is the second item. The National Crime Records Bureau released its Crime in India 2024 report, which the booklet describes as the first edition to include offences registered under a newer criminal code. The booklet also gives a short profile of the bureau, covering its origins and its place in the government. The final item recognises a warrior named Veera Pasi, who came from the Pasi community of Uttar Pradesh. Veera Pasi is remembered as a Dalit freedom fighter who took part in the Revolt of 1857 against British colonial rule, and the booklet recalls this figure's role among regional resistance heroes. Each item is short, so the section can be read in any order. The booklet presents each item under its own heading, with a few lines of description.

questions.q: Which ministry launched the National AI Skilling Initiative for the Creative Sector?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting launched the initiative in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies.

questions.q: In which year was the National Crime Records Bureau established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the National Crime Records Bureau was established in 1986.

questions.q: Under which ministry does the National Crime Records Bureau function?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the bureau functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Crime Records Bureau   ->   A. Commander under Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh
II. Indian Institute of Creative Technologies   ->   B. Includes BNS offences alongside IPC
III. Veera Pasi   ->   C. Central repository of crime and criminal data
IV. Crime in India 2024   ->   D. Implementing agency of the AI skilling initiative
Which of the following is the correct matching?
questions.explanation: The NCRB is the central repository of crime data, the institute is the implementing agency, Veera Pasi served as a commander, and the Crime in India 2024 report covers BNS offences alongside IPC.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The National Crime Records Bureau functions under the Ministry of Defence.
Reason (R): The National Crime Records Bureau acts as India's central repository of crime and criminal data.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false because the bureau functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the reason is a true statement from the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National AI Skilling Initiative for the Creative Sector is developed in partnership with Google and YouTube.
II. The NCRB's recommendations are based on the Tandon Committee and the National Police Commission.
III. The Crime in India 2024 report includes offences under the IPC only.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, whereas III is wrong because the report also covers offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The target sectors of the initiative include gaming.
II. A statue of Veera Pasi was unveiled in Raebareli.
III. Veera Pasi was a warrior from Bihar.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because Veera Pasi came from the Pasi community of Uttar Pradesh.

quizzes.title: Governance, Crime Data and Remembrance: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: The May 2026 Ailet Corner section of the booklet covers governance, crime data and remembrance. Its first item is a national initiative to build AI skills for the creative sector, launched by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The initiative aims to strengthen India's creative economy and digital content ecosystem, and its target sectors include media, animation and content creation. An institute working in creative technologies carries out the initiative, which was developed in partnership with Google and YouTube. Its objective is to build AI capabilities that are ready for industry in creative fields. The second item concerns crime data. The National Crime Records Bureau released its Crime in India 2024 report, which the booklet describes as the first edition to include offences registered under a newer criminal code. The booklet gives a short profile of the bureau, covering its origins and its place in the government. The final item recognises a warrior named Veera Pasi, who came from the Pasi community of Uttar Pradesh. Veera Pasi is remembered as a Dalit freedom fighter who took part in a major uprising against British colonial rule, and the booklet notes a recent honour for this figure in Uttar Pradesh. Each heading in the section is kept short, which makes the three items easy to scan.

questions.q: In which year was the National Crime Records Bureau established? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the National Crime Records Bureau was established in 1986.

questions.q: Under which ministry does the National Crime Records Bureau function? (ministry name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the bureau functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q: Which institute is the implementing agency of the National AI Skilling Initiative for the Creative Sector? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies as the implementing agency.

questions.q: Which commander did Veera Pasi serve under? (name of commander)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Veera Pasi served as a commander under Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh.

questions.q: In which town was a statue of Veera Pasi unveiled? (town)
questions.explanation: The booklet reports that the statue of Veera Pasi was unveiled in Raebareli.

questions.q: Along with the National Police Commission, whose recommendations form the basis of the National Crime Records Bureau? (committee name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the bureau's recommendations are based on the Tandon Committee and the National Police Commission.

questions.q: Crime in India 2024 includes offences under which new criminal law, alongside the IPC? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Crime in India 2024 report includes offences registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita alongside the IPC.
